a4.advice.b: By monitoring stress levels of your field crops and trees, we advise you on when to irrigate your plants and on the appropriate mix of soil nutrients to apply.
a4.advice.b2: This prevents you from wasting resources and damaging your crops through over-irrigation or applying the wrong fertilizers.
a4.planner.b: Our farm dashboard provides you with a daily report on your crop health, irrigation requirements, soil nutrition conditions, and local weather forecast.
a4.planner.b2: We send you a daily list of what to do to keep your plants healthy and your yields high. You can share any piece of advice by WhatsApp, Telegram or SMS with the people who work for you.
a4.trust.alt: Salad rows, figs, a field of greens, date palms and potato ridges
a4.trust.b: On average, farmers experience the following benefits from our service:
a4.trust.h: Over 6 million farmers trust us worldwide
a4.works.b: We collect over 200 parameters from satellites that monitor your farm on a daily basis, even under cloudy conditions.
a4.works.b2: Our Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, customized for your region, analyze these parameters and provide you with data-driven advice to optimize your farm operations.
a4.yields.b: We monitor biomass growth throughout the crop cycle against expected plant growth. This allows us to predict harvest yields and detect any problems.
a4.yields.b2: We advise you on corrective actions to increase crop yields, and we recommend a harvest time to maximize farm revenues.

c.crop.alfalfa.note: The heaviest water user on most Gulf farms. Judge each cut on bud stage, not on the calendar.
c.crop.apple.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.aubergine.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.banana.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.barley.note: More salt- and drought-tolerant than wheat, which is why it takes the harder ground.
c.crop.cabbage.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.carrot.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.clover.note: Measured per cut rather than per season — the water figure is the whole year.
c.crop.courgette.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.cucumber.note: Fast, shallow-rooted and unforgiving of a dry day.
c.crop.date-palm.note: Priced and monitored per tree rather than per hectare. Red palm weevil is the pest that decides whether a block survives.
c.crop.fig.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.grape.note: Open the canopy: nearly every disease on this crop is a ventilation problem first.
c.crop.guava.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.lemon.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.lime.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.maize.note: A summer crop here, and a thirsty one: it will not forgive a missed irrigation at silking.
c.crop.mango.note: Hold water back before flowering; resume once fruit has set. The crop is decided in the two weeks around bloom.
c.crop.melon.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.okra.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.olive.note: Drought-hardy, but oil yield follows the water given between flowering and stone hardening.
c.crop.onion.note: Stop watering as the tops go over, or the bulbs will not store.
c.crop.orange.note: Even irrigation prevents the repeated flushes that leaf miner rides in on.
c.crop.peach.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.pepper.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.pomegranate.note: A permanent crop: the season is the fruiting cycle, not the planting.
c.crop.potato.note: Keep moisture even once tubers start: swings are what split them.
c.crop.rhodes-grass.note: Salt-tolerant and forgiving, which is why it follows alfalfa on tired ground.
c.crop.rice.note: Winter-sown in the Gulf: heat at grain fill is what costs yield.
c.crop.sorghum.note: Winter-sown in the Gulf: heat at grain fill is what costs yield.
c.crop.squash.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.sudan-grass.note: Measured per cut rather than per season — the water figure is the whole year.
c.crop.tomato.note: Watch whitefly from the first flush — the virus it carries does more damage than the insect.
c.crop.watermelon.note: Grown through the cool months; summer plantings need shade and far more water.
c.crop.wheat.note: The region's main winter cereal. Water hardest from stem extension to grain fill; a dry spell at heading costs more than one at tillering.
c.disease.aphids.action: Spot-treat the infested edge rather than the whole field where you can — natural enemies usually catch up if they are not sprayed out.
c.disease.aphids.conditions: Mild weather and soft, heavily nitrogen-fed growth.
c.disease.aphids.name: Aphids
c.disease.aphids.prevention: Avoid over-feeding nitrogen and keep a flowering margin for the predators.
c.disease.aphids.symptoms: Colonies on new growth and leaf undersides, curled and distorted shoots, honeydew and sooty mould, and shed white skins on the leaf below.
c.disease.bayoud.action: There is no cure. Isolate the palm, stop water moving from that block to any other, and destroy the palm in place. Plant resistant varieties on that ground.
c.disease.bayoud.conditions: Soil-borne, carried on offshoots, tools and irrigation water. It does not leave a soil once it is in it.
c.disease.bayoud.name: Bayoud
c.disease.bayoud.prevention: Never bring in offshoots from an infected area. Disinfect tools between palms.
c.disease.bayoud.symptoms: One frond at a time goes white from the tip, a white stripe runs along the midrib, and the frond dies and hangs. The palm dies from one side over one or two seasons.
c.disease.black-scorch.action: Cut out affected tissue back to clean wood, burn what you remove, and treat the wound with a copper or thiophanate product. Correct the salinity that let it in.
c.disease.black-scorch.conditions: Enters through wounds, particularly after pruning or offshoot removal, and runs on in heat and salinity stress.
c.disease.black-scorch.name: Black scorch
c.disease.black-scorch.prevention: Clean tools between palms. Do not leave cut surfaces open in humid weather.
c.disease.black-scorch.symptoms: Hard black scorched patches on the leaf bases and heart, a bent or collapsed spear, and in bad cases a rotted heart that kills the palm.
c.disease.downy-mildew.action: Treat on the forecast rather than on the symptom: once the fuzz shows, a crop can be lost in a week. Alternate products by mode of action.
c.disease.downy-mildew.conditions: Needs several hours of leaf wetness under 20 °C — night irrigation and dew are what feed it.
c.disease.downy-mildew.name: Downy mildew
c.disease.downy-mildew.prevention: Irrigate early in the day, keep air moving through the crop, and do not work the crop wet.
c.disease.downy-mildew.symptoms: Angular yellow patches bounded by the leaf veins on top, grey-purple fuzz underneath in the morning. Leaves brown and die from the oldest up.
c.disease.dubas-bug.action: Spray at the nymph stage, which is the only stage that matters; adults are largely a waste of product. Thin the block to move air through it.
c.disease.dubas-bug.conditions: Two generations a year — spring and late summer. Worst in dense, poorly ventilated blocks with heavy shade.
c.disease.dubas-bug.name: Dubas bug
c.disease.dubas-bug.prevention: Thin offshoots, keep frond count sensible, and watch the undersides of the lower fronds from February.
c.disease.dubas-bug.symptoms: Sticky honeydew coating the fronds and everything under them, then black sooty mould over the sugar. Yellow speckling along the leaflets and, in a heavy year, fruit that will not fill.
c.disease.early-blight.action: Remove the worst of the lower leaves, then a protectant on a 7–10 day interval while the weather holds.
c.disease.early-blight.conditions: Warm and humid, and it takes hold fastest on a crop already short of nitrogen or water.
c.disease.early-blight.name: Early blight
c.disease.early-blight.prevention: Rotate away from solanaceous crops for two seasons, mulch to stop soil splash, and keep nitrogen adequate.
c.disease.early-blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings, like a target, on the oldest leaves first, each ringed by a yellow halo. Works up the plant as it goes.
c.disease.fusarium-wilt.action: No cure in a standing crop. Pull and remove affected plants, and stop moving soil and water from that block into clean ground.
c.disease.fusarium-wilt.conditions: Soil-borne, and it builds in ground cropped to the same family year after year. Warm soil makes it worse.
c.disease.fusarium-wilt.name: Fusarium wilt
c.disease.fusarium-wilt.prevention: Resistant rootstock or variety, long rotation, and clean irrigation water.
c.disease.fusarium-wilt.symptoms: One side of a plant wilts in the heat of the day and recovers overnight, then stops recovering. Cut the stem and the water-carrying tissue is stained brown.
c.disease.late-blight.action: Act on the forecast. Once it is in the crop, a systemic plus a protectant, and destroy badly hit plants rather than treating them.
c.disease.late-blight.conditions: Cool, wet, humid spells. It moves through a field in days, not weeks.
c.disease.late-blight.name: Late blight
c.disease.late-blight.prevention: Certified seed, generous hilling on potatoes, and no cull piles left near the field.
c.disease.late-blight.symptoms: Dark greasy patches on leaves and stems with a pale margin, white mould underneath in humid air, and a brown marbled rot in the tuber or fruit.
c.disease.leaf-miner.action: Time any treatment to the flush, not the calendar. Systemic products work; contact sprays do not reach a larva inside the leaf.
c.disease.leaf-miner.conditions: Flushes of soft new growth in warm weather — citrus after summer irrigation is the classic case.
c.disease.leaf-miner.name: Leaf miner
c.disease.leaf-miner.prevention: Even out irrigation and nitrogen so the tree flushes once rather than repeatedly.
c.disease.leaf-miner.symptoms: Silver winding tunnels inside the leaf, curled and hardened young citrus leaves, and mines that open the leaf to canker.
c.disease.mango-anthracnose.action: Protectant sprays through flowering, and handle fruit carefully — most post-harvest rot starts as a bruise.
c.disease.mango-anthracnose.conditions: Humidity and rain at flowering. Most of the damage is decided in the two weeks around bloom.
c.disease.mango-anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
c.disease.mango-anthracnose.prevention: Prune out dead wood, which is where it overwinters, and avoid wetting the canopy at bloom.
c.disease.mango-anthracnose.symptoms: Black sunken spots on leaves, flowers and fruit, flower panicles that blacken and drop, and fruit that rots at the stem end after picking.
c.disease.mango-hopper.action: Treat at first flowering, before fruit set, and again if tapping a panicle still scatters adults.
c.disease.mango-hopper.conditions: Flowering, in warm still weather. A heavy year can take most of the crop before anyone notices the insect.
c.disease.mango-hopper.name: Mango hopper
c.disease.mango-hopper.prevention: Keep the canopy open and do not let dense old wood build up in the centre.
c.disease.mango-hopper.symptoms: Wedge-shaped insects that scatter when a panicle is tapped, sticky honeydew over the leaves, and flower panicles that dry and drop without setting.
c.disease.olive-fruit-fly.action: Bait traps to find the first flight, then treat on threshold rather than on the calendar. Harvest promptly once numbers climb.
c.disease.olive-fruit-fly.conditions: From fruit set onward, worst where summers are mild and irrigation keeps the fruit soft.
c.disease.olive-fruit-fly.name: Olive fruit fly
c.disease.olive-fruit-fly.prevention: Remove and destroy dropped fruit; do not leave an unharvested tree as a nursery.
c.disease.olive-fruit-fly.symptoms: A small sting mark on the fruit, then a tunnel and a brown rot inside it. Fruit drops early and oil turns acidic.
c.disease.olive-peacock-spot.action: Copper after the main leaf fall and again before flowering. Open the centre of the tree so it dries faster after dew.
c.disease.olive-peacock-spot.conditions: Cool, wet spells with long leaf wetness — the tail of winter into spring.
c.disease.olive-peacock-spot.name: Peacock spot
c.disease.olive-peacock-spot.prevention: Prune for light and air, and clear fallen leaves from under the tree.
c.disease.olive-peacock-spot.symptoms: Dark rings with a yellow halo on the upper leaf surface, like a peacock's eye, then heavy leaf fall from the bottom of the tree up.
c.disease.powdery-mildew.action: Sulphur where the temperature allows it, or an approved systemic on rotation so resistance does not build. Open the canopy up.
c.disease.powdery-mildew.conditions: Warm days, cool nights and high humidity without free water on the leaf — which is why it follows a run of heavy dew.
c.disease.powdery-mildew.name: Powdery mildew
c.disease.powdery-mildew.prevention: Wider spacing, morning irrigation rather than evening, and a variety with resistance where one exists.
c.disease.powdery-mildew.symptoms: White dusty patches on the upper leaf surface first, spreading until leaves yellow and drop. Fruit under bare leaves scalds.
c.disease.red-palm-weevil.action: Report it — this is a quarantine pest in the GCC. Inject the trunk with an approved systemic, avoid pruning in flight season, and seal every cut. Severely infested palms must be removed and destroyed, not moved.
c.disease.red-palm-weevil.conditions: Spreads year round, fastest in spring and autumn. Adults are drawn to fresh cuts, so pruning wounds and offshoot removal are the usual way in.
c.disease.red-palm-weevil.name: Red palm weevil
c.disease.red-palm-weevil.prevention: Do not prune between March and May. Paint or seal cuts the same day. Keep pheromone traps at the block edge, not among the palms.
c.disease.red-palm-weevil.symptoms: Chewing sounds inside the trunk, oozing brown sap with a fermented smell, tunnels at the leaf bases, and fronds that wilt and collapse from the crown. A palm can be hollow before anything shows outside.
c.disease.root-rot.action: Correct the watering first — a fungicide on saturated ground buys nothing. Then treat with an approved product if the block warrants it.
c.disease.root-rot.conditions: Over-irrigation and poor drainage, above all in heavy ground or where a pan holds water in the root zone.
c.disease.root-rot.name: Root rot
c.disease.root-rot.prevention: Water to the root depth and no further, and break any pan that is holding water.
c.disease.root-rot.symptoms: Plants that look short of water while the soil is wet, yellowing from the bottom, and roots that are brown, soft and easily stripped.
c.disease.spider-mite.action: A miticide with a different mode of action from the last one used, covering the leaf undersides. Predatory mites where the crop allows.
c.disease.spider-mite.conditions: Hot, dry and dusty — a GCC summer is their season, and dust on a field edge is where an outbreak usually starts.
c.disease.spider-mite.name: Two-spotted spider mite
c.disease.spider-mite.prevention: Keep dust down on tracks, avoid drought stress, and do not overuse broad-spectrum insecticides, which remove the predators first.
c.disease.spider-mite.symptoms: Fine pale stippling across the leaf, going bronze, with webbing in the growing points when it is bad. Turn a leaf over to find them.
c.disease.whitefly.action: Treat while numbers are low, rotating modes of action; once a virus is in the crop the insect is the only thing left to control.
c.disease.whitefly.conditions: Warm weather and a year-round host nearby. Numbers build through autumn.
c.disease.whitefly.name: Whitefly
c.disease.whitefly.prevention: Clear a host-free break between crops, use yellow sticky traps to see the build-up early, and screen nursery stock.
c.disease.whitefly.symptoms: A cloud of small white insects when the crop is disturbed, sticky honeydew and sooty mould below, and leaves that curl and yellow. Often the virus it carries does the real damage.

c.glossary.active-ingredient-ai.definiti: The chemical component of a pesticide or fertiliser that produces the desired effect, listed as a percentage of the total product formulation.
c.glossary.canopy.definition: The upper layer of leaves and branches of a plant or crop that intercepts light and water; canopy density and structure are key to photosynthesis and disease risk.
c.glossary.crop-coefficient-kc.definitio: A multiplier that adjusts reference ET for your specific crop, accounting for its height, leaf area, and growth stage; Kc ranges from 0.3 to 1.2 or higher depending on crop type and stage.
c.glossary.crop-cycle.definition: The complete growing period from sowing or planting to harvest for a single crop, including germination, vegetative growth, flowering, and maturity stages.
c.glossary.dunum.definition: A traditional unit of land area used in the Middle East and Central Asia, equal to 1,000 square metres or 0.1 hectares; also spelled 'donum' or 'decare'.
c.glossary.evapotranspiration-et.definit: The total amount of water lost from soil and plants to the atmosphere through evaporation and plant transpiration, measured in millimetres per day or per season.
c.glossary.fertigation.definition: The delivery of fertiliser through irrigation water, allowing precise, frequent nutrient application in small doses directly to the root zone.
c.glossary.measure.definition: A satellite-derived index (NDVI, NDWI, NDRE, EVI, MSAVI, PSRI) that quantifies a specific crop health attribute; each measure has a range and a colour-coded scale.
c.glossary.plot.definition: A sub-division of a field, usually uniform in soil type, crop, or management practice; plots allow you to track variation within a field and compare different treatments or zones.
c.glossary.pre-harvest-interval-phi.defi: The minimum number of days that must pass between the last application of a pesticide and harvest, set to ensure residues decay to safe levels.
c.glossary.re-entry-interval-rei.definit: The minimum hours or days workers must wait before re-entering a sprayed field without protective equipment, designed to protect worker health from pesticide exposure.
c.glossary.reference-et-et0.definition: The baseline evapotranspiration rate for a hypothetical grass reference crop under optimal conditions, used as a standard to compare water needs across different crops and regions.
c.glossary.vigour.definition: The overall strength and growth rate of a plant or crop, assessed by biomass accumulation, leaf colour, and development speed; vigour correlates with yield potential.
c.glossary.water-stress.definition: A condition where plant water demand exceeds supply, reducing photosynthesis, growth, and yield; detected by lower soil moisture, leaf wilting, or lower NDWI values.
c.help.add-farm.body.0: To start using Wafra, you need to add at least one farm. A farm is your top-level unit — its boundary holds the plots and the trees inside it. You can add a farm either by searching for it on the map or by drawing its boundary yourself. If you import cadastral data, Wafra can help you match it to the map.
c.help.add-farm.body.1: Precise field boundaries help Wafra deliver accurate satellite data, advice, and reports for each plot. You can draw them freehand, load them from a file, or refine them later. Boundaries are stored in your farm record and can be edited or updated any time.
c.help.add-farm.body.2: Once your farm is added, you can draw its plots or send the boundary for a survey, invite your team, and begin receiving advice.
c.help.add-farm.steps.0: From the home screen, tap or click 'Add farm'.
c.help.add-farm.steps.1: Enter your farm name and select your country and region.
c.help.add-farm.steps.2: On the map, tap 'Draw' and outline your farm boundary by clicking points around the perimeter. Use pinch-to-zoom for precision.
c.help.add-farm.steps.3: Tap 'Done' to save your farm. You can refine the boundary later if needed.
c.help.add-farm.steps.4: You can now add plots and crops.
c.help.add-farm.summary: Register your farm and mark its edges on the map.
c.help.add-farm.title: How to add a farm and draw a boundary
c.help.advice-inbox.body.0: Your Advice inbox receives notifications about weather, disease risk, soil moisture, nutrients, and more. Advice is categorised by urgency and type so you can prioritise.
c.help.advice-inbox.body.1: Urgent advice (red) needs action within a few days. Action-needed advice (yellow) should be done within the week. Routine advice (blue) is informational and can be scheduled flexibly.
c.help.advice-inbox.body.2: You can filter by farm, plot, type or status. Archive advice once you have acted or decided not to act. Your team members will also receive relevant advice if they have permission.
c.help.advice-inbox.summary: How to read, filter, and act on Wafra's recommendations.
c.help.advice-inbox.title: Using the advice inbox to stay informed
c.help.contact-wafra.body.0: From any screen in Wafra, tap the help icon or go to Settings > Help to see the user guide, FAQs, and support options. You can email support, submit a support ticket, or request a call with an agronomist.
c.help.contact-wafra.body.1: Wafra's support team is available in your language and can help with technical issues, questions about your plan, or advice on features. Response times are guaranteed on Pro.
c.help.contact-wafra.body.2: You can also report bugs or suggest features directly from Settings > Feedback.
c.help.contact-wafra.summary: How to get in touch with support, report a bug, or request a feature.
c.help.contact-wafra.title: Contacting Wafra for help
c.help.field-observation.body.0: A field observation is a quick scouting visit where you record what you see — pest damage, disease symptoms, growth stage, water stress signs, or anything unusual. Observations become part of your farm record and help Wafra refine its forecasts.
c.help.field-observation.body.1: You can take photos, note the affected area, and tag the observation with tags like 'disease', 'pest', 'weed', or 'nutrition'. Your team can see and comment on observations in real time.
c.help.field-observation.body.2: Combine observations with weather data and satellite imagery for a complete picture of what is happening in your field.
c.help.field-observation.steps.0: From your farm or field view, tap 'Observation' or 'Scout'.
c.help.field-observation.steps.3: Add a title like 'Powdery mildew spotted on leaves'.
c.help.field-observation.steps.4: Select tags (disease, pest, weed, vigour, other).
c.help.field-observation.steps.5: Add notes and severity (mild, moderate, severe).
c.help.field-observation.summary: How to record observations, photos, and measurements from the field.
c.help.field-observation.title: Taking a field observation (scouting report)
c.help.health-scale.body.0: Wafra uses a four-state scale to summarise crop health: Strong (green), Fair (yellow), Poor (orange), and Severe (red). This scale combines multiple measures — NDVI, water stress, nutrients, and more — into one easy visual.
c.help.health-scale.body.1: Strong means your crop is developing well and needs only routine attention. Fair means watch closely and plan for adjustments. Poor means you should act within days. Severe means urgent intervention is needed.
c.help.health-scale.body.2: The scale changes as your crop grows and as conditions change. Check your dashboard daily during the growing season to catch problems early.
c.help.health-scale.summary: What the colour codes and symbols mean for your crops.
c.help.health-scale.title: Understanding the four-state health scale
c.help.invite-team.body.0: A farm has an owner and one supervisor. The owner manages the subscription and the settings and decides what gets done; the supervisor receives the work, closes it off and can review reports and edit farm data.
c.help.invite-team.body.1: To invite someone, enter their phone number or email and select their role. They will receive an invitation, accept it, and be added to the farm. You can change roles or remove team members any time.
c.help.invite-team.body.2: Roles are per farm. A person can be the supervisor on one farm and have no access to another.
c.help.invite-team.steps.0: From Settings or Farm settings, tap 'Team' or 'Invite member'.
c.help.invite-team.steps.1: Enter the email address or phone number.
c.help.invite-team.steps.2: Select the farm. Anyone you invite joins as its supervisor.
c.help.invite-team.steps.3: Add a personal message if you like.
c.help.invite-team.steps.5: They will receive an email or SMS and can join.
c.help.invite-team.summary: How to add team members and control what they can do.
c.help.invite-team.title: Inviting your team and managing roles
c.help.language-units.body.0: Wafra is available in English, Arabic, French, Spanish, and Mandarin. You can change your language any time in Settings. Your language preference is saved to your account, so it will follow you across devices.
c.help.language-units.body.1: You can also choose your preferred units — metres or feet for distance, Celsius or Fahrenheit for temperature, and cubic metres or gallons for water volume. These choices are saved with your account.
c.help.language-units.steps.2: Tap 'Units' and select your preferred units for distance and temperature.
c.help.language-units.summary: How to switch language, temperature units, and distance units.
c.help.language-units.title: Changing your language and units
c.help.offline-work.body.0: Wafra lets you work offline on your phone or tablet. You can record what you did about a piece of advice, take observations, record diary entries, and review cached data — all without an internet connection. When you reconnect, Wafra syncs automatically.
c.help.offline-work.body.1: Before going offline, make sure you have downloaded the latest farm data and weather forecast. On a phone, this is called 'Cache' or 'Offline mode'. On a desktop, offline features are more limited.
c.help.offline-work.body.2: Offline work includes: reading your farm, recording what you did with photos, recording observations and diary entries, and scouting. You cannot send advice to your supervisor, edit plot boundaries, or invite anyone offline.
c.help.offline-work.steps.0: Before leaving the office, open Settings and tap 'Offline mode' or 'Cache data'.
c.help.offline-work.steps.2: On your phone, you can now work offline.
c.help.offline-work.steps.3: When back online, open Wafra and tap 'Sync'.
c.help.offline-work.steps.4: All your entries are uploaded and merged into the farm record.
c.help.offline-work.summary: How to use Wafra without internet and sync when you reconnect.
c.help.offline-work.title: Working offline and syncing later
c.help.plan-locked.body.0: Wafra has two levels for each service. Basic includes the essentials — farm mapping, health and water stress, weather, advice, offline work, and satellite imagery at 10-metre resolution. Pro adds 1-metre imagery, irrigation scheduling and fertigation, growth stages and yield forecasting, disease forecasting, the irrigation efficiency map, and soil nutrient reports.
c.help.plan-locked.body.1: Some features are locked on Basic and need Pro. A lock icon shows you which. Every account gets 30 days free on whichever level it picks, and you can change level at any time.
c.help.plan-locked.body.2: All plans include five languages, multi-user roles, 24/7 support, and offline work.
c.help.plan-locked.summary: What is included on Basic and on Pro.
c.help.plan-locked.title: Understanding your plan and what is locked
c.help.record-actions.body.0: The farm diary is your record of all inputs and activities. Log every spray, fertiliser application, irrigation event, and harvest. This creates a complete audit trail for your farm and helps Wafra learn what works best for you.
c.help.record-actions.body.1: Each entry includes the date, plot, crop, product or action, quantity, and notes. You can also attach photos. Wafra uses this data to forecast disease risk, optimise nutrients, and generate reports.
c.help.record-actions.body.2: Recording is quick — most entries take 30 seconds. Do it as you work or review the day in the evening.
c.help.record-actions.steps.0: From the farm view, tap 'Diary' or 'Activity log'.
c.help.record-actions.steps.1: Tap 'Add entry' and select the entry type (spray, fertiliser, irrigation, harvest, other).
c.help.record-actions.steps.2: Fill in the plot, crop, date, product, quantity, and notes.
c.help.record-actions.summary: How to log your activities, sprays, fertiliser, and irrigation.
c.help.record-actions.title: Recording what you did (farm diary)
c.help.roles-explained.body.0: Owner can do everything — add farms, invite team, change the subscription, view all reports, and manage settings. If you are the farm owner, you are an Owner by default.
c.help.roles-explained.body.1: A supervisor can view all farm data, record what was done about a piece of advice, create observations and diary entries, and generate reports. Supervisors cannot send advice, change the subscription or invite anyone.
c.help.roles-explained.body.2: Nobody below the supervisor holds an account. Work reaches the people who do it as a message with a link they tap when it is done, which is how a farm of five men gets by without five logins.
c.help.roles-explained.summary: A breakdown of what an owner can do and what a supervisor can do.
c.help.roles-explained.title: Roles and what each can do
c.help.what-measures-mean.body.0: Wafra displays six satellite-derived measures. Each tells you something different about your crop. NDVI is overall health and vigour. NDWI is water stress — high NDWI (closer to 1) means plenty of water, low means stress. NDRE is nutrition, mainly nitrogen. EVI is growth momentum and biomass. MSAVI is similar to NDVI but corrected for soil background. PSRI is photosynthetic efficiency.
c.help.what-measures-mean.body.1: You do not need to be an expert to use these. Read the tooltips and follow the advice. If a measure shows poor values, the advice engine will alert you and suggest action.
c.help.what-measures-mean.body.2: Pro unlocks time series, the growth-stage curve, and comparison tools to dig deeper.
c.help.what-measures-mean.summary: A plain explanation of NDVI, NDWI, NDRE, EVI, MSAVI, and PSRI.
c.help.what-measures-mean.title: What each measure means and why it matters

c.measure.evi.help: Tracks vigour and biomass as the crop builds it, corrected for the soil behind it, so you can follow growth momentum and development stages.
c.measure.moisture.help: Shows how much water the root zone is holding, read from radar that sees through cloud, so you can water before the crop feels it rather than after.
c.measure.ndre.help: Shows nutrient content, nitrogen above all, so you can adjust fertiliser timing and rates to protect the yield.
c.measure.ndvi.help: Shows the overall photosynthetic activity and vegetation density of your crop, so stress, vigour and growth variability show up early.
c.measure.ndwi.help: Shows the water held in leaves and soil, so you can see where the crop is short of water and when irrigation matters most.

legal.p1: We hold your name, mobile number, the farms you add and the work recorded against them.
legal.p2: Photographs taken in the field record where and when they were taken and who took them. Your supervisor and the farm owner can see them. We do not track anyone’s position at any other time.
legal.p3: Photographs are served through short-lived private links. A link that leaks stops working.
legal.p4: You can ask us to delete your personal data. Advice records are kept for seven years with your personal details removed.
legal.t1: Everything this app tells you about your crop is decision support. It is advice, not a prescription.
legal.t2: You remain responsible for what is applied on your land. Complying with local pesticide regulation rests with whoever applies the product.
legal.t3: Satellite measurements can be affected by cloud, dust and the timing of a pass. Where we cannot measure something we say so rather than estimating it.
legal.t4: Subscriptions are billed through the App Store or Google Play and renew until you cancel there.
